sci.sky.moon-phases.L5.7: A picture of the Sun taken from a solar observatory. Observatories have photographed the Sun on clear days for more than a hundred years.

sci.sky.moons-asteroids-comets.L3.0: Shooting stars on the Geminid nights, around 13 and 14 December, from a terrace or a dark beach.
sci.sky.moons-asteroids-comets.L3.2: A round lake inside a crater made by a meteorite, in a picture.
sci.sky.moons-asteroids-comets.L3.3: Meteorites on display in a museum or science centre.

sci.sky.solar-system.L4.4: A round lake in a crater about 1.8 kilometres wide, made by a space rock long ago, in a picture.

sci.sky.solar-system.L5.6: A planetarium show, with the planets and moons projected on a dome.

sci.sky.stargazing.L1.0: On every full Moon night, thousands of people walk round a sacred hill by moonlight.
sci.sky.stargazing.L1.1: Children sing 'Nila nila odi vaa', asking the Moon to come running. The Moon is also called Uncle Moon.
sci.sky.stargazing.L1.3: On Kojagiri Purnima, families stay up to see the full Moon and drink warm masala milk.
sci.sky.stargazing.L1.4: On the full Moon night after Durga Puja, families keep Kojagori Lakshmi Puja.
sci.sky.stargazing.L1.5: At the end of Ramzan, people look for the thin new crescent Moon before Eid begins.
sci.sky.stargazing.L1.6: A dark sky far from town lights, where the Milky Way shines over the hills.

sci.sky.stargazing.L3.6: Arundhati being spoken of at weddings, as a star always beside her husband Vasishtha.

sci.sky.sun-moon-stars.L1.0: At Pongal, families cook sweet pongal outside in the morning sunshine, to thank the Sun for the harvest.
sci.sky.sun-moon-stars.L1.1: At Chhath Puja, people stand in rivers and ponds at sunset and sunrise to greet the Sun.
sci.sky.sun-moon-stars.L1.2: A temple built like a giant chariot for the Sun, with huge stone wheels, in a picture.
sci.sky.sun-moon-stars.L1.3: On Sharad Purnima, many families sit out under the full Moon and share sweet milk.
sci.sky.sun-moon-stars.L1.4: Far from town lights, the night sky is full of stars.
sci.sky.sun-moon-stars.L1.5: On rooftops, people spread coconut pieces and chillies on mats to dry in the sun.
sci.sky.sun-moon-stars.L1.6: A dark-sky place, where lights are kept low so the stars can be seen.

sci.sky.the-sun.L3.2: A building or an airport with solar panels on its roof, running on the Sun's power.
sci.sky.the-sun.L3.3: Salt pans by the sea, where the Sun dries seawater into salt.
sci.sky.the-sun.L3.4: A sweet and sour mango pickle that is cooked slowly by the Sun in glass jars on a terrace.
sci.sky.the-sun.L3.5: Pongal and Makar Sankranti, when families give thanks for the harvest and the Sun. Chhath, when families pray to the Sun at sunrise and sunset.
sci.sky.the-sun.L3.6: A temple built as the Sun's chariot, with great stone wheels, in a picture.

sci.sky.the-sun.L4.0: The thin pink-red rim and silvery glow round the black Moon in pictures of a total solar eclipse.
sci.sky.the-sun.L4.1: Solar panels on apartment roofs, tilted towards the south.
sci.sky.the-sun.L4.5: A solar observatory that has been recording the Sun since 1899, in a picture.

sci.sound.hearing.L1.0: A koel calling 'ku-oo' from a tree on a hot summer morning, heard from inside the flat.
sci.sound.hearing.L1.1: A woman selling greens calling 'Keerai! Keerai!' as she walks down a street, getting softer as she goes.
sci.sound.hearing.L1.2: Bihu drums heard from many streets away before the dancers come into sight.
sci.sound.hearing.L1.3: A ship's horn at a port, heard across the harbour.
sci.sound.hearing.L1.4: A street dog lifting and turning her ears towards a sound before anyone else has heard it.

sci.sound.hearing.L3.0: A traffic policeman at a busy junction, standing in the noise of horns all day.
sci.sound.hearing.L3.3: Your ears popping in a lift or on a ghat road.

sci.sound.music.L2.1: The chenda drums at a temple festival, with many drummers keeping one beat.
sci.sound.music.L2.2: The dhakis playing the big dhak drum during Durga Puja.

sci.sound.sound-moves.L1.0: Vegetable and fish sellers walk down the street calling out what they sell. People hear them from the fourth and fifth floors of a building.
sci.sound.sound-moves.L1.1: During the monsoon, families see the lightning over the sea first and hear the thunder a few moments later.
sci.sound.sound-moves.L1.2: At Ganesh Chaturthi, cone-shaped loudspeakers on poles send music and announcements along the street.
sci.sound.sound-moves.L1.3: During Durga Puja, people blow the conch shell, and the sound carries across the whole neighbourhood.
sci.sound.sound-moves.L1.4: At night, in towns and villages, people hear a train horn from a station far away.

sci.sound.sources-of-sound.L1.0: At a temple festival, long rows of drummers play the chenda together, and the sound fills the town.
sci.sound.sources-of-sound.L1.1: During Durga Puja, drummers play the dhak, a big drum hung from the shoulder.
sci.sound.sources-of-sound.L1.2: In summer, the koel calls 'koo-ooo' loudly from trees in the city. The loud caller is the male, a black bird with red eyes.
sci.sound.sources-of-sound.L1.3: At Bohag Bihu, people play the dhol and blow the pepa, a pipe made from a buffalo horn.

sci.sound.vibration.L5.1: A mridangam player at a concert, pressing a hand on the skin to stop a note short.
sci.sound.vibration.L5.5: A kite string humming in the wind at Uttarayan or at Pongal.
sci.sound.vibration.L5.6: The nadaswaram and the thavil at a wedding: one is an air column, the other has two skins.

sci.sound.waves.L3.1: Waves on any beach, with a fishing boat bobbing far out.
sci.sound.waves.L3.3: A paddy field with waves running across it in the wind.
sci.sound.waves.L3.4: The tsunami warning signs and evacuation route boards along the coast.

sci.sound.waves.L4.4: Sea waves arriving one after another on a beach. Count the seconds between two waves.

sci.space-time.dimensions.L2.0: A kolam or rangoli at a doorway is made of flat shapes: dots, lines, circles and triangles.
sci.space-time.dimensions.L2.1: A round biscuit tin is a cylinder. Its top and bottom are flat circles, and its side is curved.
sci.space-time.dimensions.L2.3: A cut onion in a kitchen shows rings: flat circles inside circles.
sci.space-time.dimensions.L2.4: A temple gopuram is a solid built in layers, each layer a little smaller than the one below.

sci.space-time.space.L2.0: A tall temple gopuram looks small from far across the city, and huge when you stand at its gate.
sci.space-time.space.L2.1: Railway tracks at a station seem to come together far away, though they stay the same distance apart. That is because far things look smaller, and so does the gap between the rails.
sci.space-time.space.L2.2: Crows or pigeons on a wire sit with gaps between them, keeping some space for each bird.
sci.space-time.space.L2.3: A plane in the sky looks as small as a bird, though it is very big.
sci.space-time.space.L2.4: At night from a terrace, the Moon looks about as wide as a small pea held at arm's length, and the stars look like tiny dots.

sci.space-time.time.L2.0: A big old clock tower chiming over the city.
sci.space-time.time.L2.1: A giant stone sundial whose shadow moves as you watch. Any sundial in a park will do.
sci.space-time.time.L2.3: The pressure cooker whistling on a stove, while someone counts the whistles.

sci.states.crystals.L3.1: Kalkandu, rock sugar, given at a temple as prasadam.
sci.states.crystals.L3.2: White salt heaps at salt pans along a coast, seen from the road.

sci.states.dissolving.L3.4: White salt heaps beside shallow pans on the coast.

sci.states.evaporation-and-condensation..5: Winter fog in the city, and morning mist in the hills.

sci.states.evaporation-and-condensation..4: Dew on the seat of a parked scooter on a winter morning.

sci.states.floating-and-sinking.L2.0: Round boats made of woven bamboo, carrying people across a river.
sci.states.floating-and-sinking.L2.1: Houseboats made of wood, floating on the backwaters.
sci.states.floating-and-sinking.L2.2: Floating islands of plants, soil and roots on a lake, in a picture or a video.
sci.states.floating-and-sinking.L2.3: Clay Ganesha and Durga idols sinking in water after festivals. Clay is heavier than the water that would fill the same space.
sci.states.floating-and-sinking.L2.4: Fishing nets on a beach, with a row of floats along the top edge.

sci.states.liquids-up-close.L4.4: A dam, a thick wall across a river.
sci.states.liquids-up-close.L4.8: A step well, with deep steps down to the water.

sci.states.melting-and-solidifying.L2.0: Fish packed in crushed ice at a fish market. The ice melts slowly and keeps the fish cold.
sci.states.melting-and-solidifying.L2.1: A goldsmith melting gold in a small cup over a hot flame, then pouring it into a mould.
sci.states.melting-and-solidifying.L2.4: A kulfi cart, with kulfi cones packed in a pot of ice and salt.

sci.states.particles.L3.4: Salt pans by the sea, where sea water dries in the sun and the dissolved salt comes back as white crystals.

sci.states.solids-liquids-gases.L2.0: Kulfi set in cone-shaped moulds at a kulfi cart. The milk took the shape of the mould, then froze.
sci.states.solids-liquids-gases.L2.1: Steam cooking idlis in an idli pot in a kitchen.
sci.states.solids-liquids-gases.L2.2: Coconut water inside a tender coconut at a stall, taking the shape of the inside of the nut.
sci.states.solids-liquids-gases.L2.3: Tall cones of ice that farmers build in winter, in a picture. They melt slowly in spring and water the fields.
sci.states.solids-liquids-gases.L2.4: Morning fog over the hills. It is tiny drops of liquid water floating in the air.

sci.story-of-universe.black-holes.L3.2: A railway tunnel on a hill section, looking black inside at noon.
sci.story-of-universe.black-holes.L3.4: A sky show about black holes at a planetarium.
sci.story-of-universe.black-holes.L3.5: News about a gravitational-wave detector, an instrument that catches ripples from far-off black holes.

sci.story-of-universe.galaxies-and-big-b.3: A picture of big radio telescope dishes, which pick up radio waves from far galaxies.

sci.story-of-universe.galaxies.L3.5: A planetarium show that shows the Milky Way as it looks from a dark sky.

sci.waste.compost-and-disposal.L3.1: Stacked terracotta compost pots on balconies.

sci.waste.sorting-waste.L2.1: The waste collector's cart or truck with two drums or two parts.

sci.waste.sorting-waste.L3.2: Women in green uniforms collecting dry waste from homes.

sci.water.water-cycle.L3.3: Thick winter fog over the city and the fields, when trains and flights run late.
sci.water.water-cycle.L3.4: Clouds sitting on the hills in the monsoon.
sci.water.water-cycle.L3.5: Salt pans beside the road near the sea, with white heaps of salt.

sci.water.water-sources-and-uses.L1.0: A row of plastic and steel pots lined up at a public tap, waiting for the water to come.
sci.water.water-sources-and-uses.L1.1: A red clay matka of drinking water under a tree in a street, for anyone who is thirsty.
sci.water.water-sources-and-uses.L1.2: A round well in the courtyard of an old house, with a rope and a bucket.
sci.water.water-sources-and-uses.L1.3: A stepwell, with steps going far down to the water.
sci.water.water-sources-and-uses.L1.4: Floating islands of plants on a lake, where fishers live on the water, in a picture.

sci.water.water-sources-and-uses.L3.4: An old stepwell, with steps going down to the water.

sci.water.water-sources-and-uses.L5.5: Salt pans seen from a train window, with white heaps of salt beside shallow ponds.

sci.weather.clouds-and-rain.L2.0: Clouds sitting on the hills during the monsoon.
sci.weather.clouds-and-rain.L2.1: A very rainy hill town, in the news or on a map. Some of the rainiest places on Earth are hill towns where the clouds pile up.
sci.weather.clouds-and-rain.L2.3: Dark grey clouds over the sea in November, before a northeast monsoon storm.
sci.weather.clouds-and-rain.L2.4: Fog on a winter morning. Fog is a cloud that sits on the ground.

sci.weather.forecasting.L3.0: The weather report after the news on television, with a map and cloud symbols.
sci.weather.forecasting.L3.2: Fishing boats pulled high up on the beach when a storm warning is given.
sci.weather.forecasting.L3.4: Tall storm clouds building over the city on an April or May afternoon.

sci.weather.weather.L1.2: Tea-pickers on a hillside with plastic sheets over their heads and backs in the rain.

sci.weather.wind-and-air.L3.3: Rows of wind turbines along a highway.

sci.what-is-life.cells-divide.L5.1: Sugarcane setts being planted in a field. Each sett is a piece of cane with two or three nodes.
sci.what-is-life.cells-divide.L5.5: Skin peeling from your shoulders a few days after a sunny day at the beach.

sci.what-is-life.edge-of-life.L5.3: At the beach, every handful of sea water holds millions of phages and the bacteria they infect.

sci.what-is-life.inside-a-cell.L5.2: The pink and white nithyakalyani flowers by a roadside, the plant that gave a medicine which stops microtubules.
sci.what-is-life.inside-a-cell.L5.6: Corals in an aquarium or a video. Tiny algae live inside the coral animal's cells and share the food they make from sunlight.

sci.what-is-life.signs-of-life.L1.3: Snails on wet walls and pots during the monsoon.

sci.what-is-life.signs-of-life.L2.1: Rain tree leaves folded up on an evening walk along a road.
sci.what-is-life.signs-of-life.L2.4: A coconut lying in a backyard, with a green shoot growing out of the husk.

sci.what-is-life.signs-of-life.L3.5: Your breath making a little cloud on a cold winter morning.

sci.what-is-real.consciousness.L2.0: In a flat, everyone notices the sudden quiet when the fan stops in a power cut.
sci.what-is-real.consciousness.L2.1: A flower seller in a busy market hears her own name through all the noise.
sci.what-is-real.consciousness.L2.2: A crow on a balcony turns her head the moment a steel plate clinks.
sci.what-is-real.consciousness.L2.3: A tulsi plant on a windowsill leans towards the light.
sci.what-is-real.consciousness.L2.4: In many homes, mothers say they sleep through thunder but wake at their baby's small cry.

sci.what-is-real.perception-and-reality..0: Pressure cooker whistles from neighbouring flats at breakfast and lunch time.
sci.what-is-real.perception-and-reality..1: A shimmering 'puddle' on a hot road in summer that dries up as you get close: a mirage, seen on highways.
sci.what-is-real.perception-and-reality..2: Kites rising on Makar Sankranti over rooftops, lifted by wind nobody can see.
sci.what-is-real.perception-and-reality..3: Coconut palms bending and rustling near the coast before the monsoon rain arrives.
